land.text: the islands claimed by the United Provinces of the River Plate in 1820 and settled by Vernet, whose garrison 'departed without a fight on 5 January' 1833

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Río de la Plata row ends in 1833 and shows no Falklands; the page names the United Provinces of the River Plate.

capitals.name: Port Louis (Anson's Harbour from 1841)
capitals.note: The page puts the first British resident at Vernet's settlement at Port Louis (January 1834) and the first Lieutenant Governor at Anson's Harbour (October 1841). Port Louis is not in the gazetteer and its coordinates are approximate; the move date is not given.

capitals.name: Stanley (Port Stanley)
capitals.note: "In July 1845, at Moody's suggestion, the new capital of the islands was officially named Port Stanley"; construction began in July 1843.

correction.text: the archipelago: 'East Falkland, West Falkland, and 776 smaller islands', 'with an area of 4,700 sq mi (12,000 km2)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Falkland row (the British Colonial Empire row is an aggregate). Infobox area 12,173 km2; the gazetteer resolves the Falkland Islands to 47 cells, about 11,900 km2 (ratio 0.98). South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands were governed as dependencies 1908-1985 (ledger) and are not in this shape.

region.text: the Falkland Islands: 'Captain James Onslow, of the brig-sloop HMS Clio, arrived at Vernet's settlement at Port Louis' on 3 January 1833

ledger.note: 3 January 1833: Britain reasserts its rule. 'On 3 January 1833, Captain James Onslow, of the brig-sloop HMS Clio, arrived at Vernet's settlement at Port Louis'; the Argentine commander 'departed without a fight on 5 January'. Infobox 'British rule reasserted: 3 January 1833'.

1841-1843: the islands become a Crown colony. 'In May 1840, the British Government made the decision to colonise the Falkland Islands'; Moody, the first Lieutenant Governor, arrived in October 1841 and the post was 'renamed Governor of the Falkland Islands in 1843'. No change of land.

July 1845: the capital is named Port Stanley. 'In July 1845, at Moody's suggestion, the new capital of the islands was officially named Port Stanley'; 'construction of the new settlement started in July 1843'.

region.text: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, governed as part of 'the Falkland Islands Dependencies starting in 1908'

ledger.note: 1908: the Falkland Islands Dependencies are created. 'The Falklands governed these territories as the Falkland Islands Dependencies starting in 1908.' The Falkland page does not list the members; South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands are named by the History page for 1985.

region.text: the Falkland Islands, invaded by Argentina

ledger.note: 2 April 1982: Argentina invades the Falklands. 'Argentina invaded the islands on 2 April 1982, using special forces.' Infobox 'occupation 2 April to 14 June 1982'.
14 June 1982: the Argentine garrison surrenders. The British 'forced the Argentine garrison to surrender on 14 June 1982'; 'British administration was restored two months later'.

region.text: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, separate from the Falkland Islands

ledger.note: 1985: the Falkland Islands Dependency is dissolved. 'In 1985, the Falkland Islands Dependency was split into the Falkland Islands proper' and South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, which became a separate territory.

wars.name: Falklands War
wars.outcome: British victory: the Argentine invasion of 2 April 1982 is reversed when the garrison surrenders on 14 June 1982; the UK 'ruled out further talks over the islands' sovereignty'.
wars.note: The sovereignty of the islands remains disputed: Argentina has reaffirmed its claim (Menem, 1998). The United Kingdom belligerent is kingdom-of-great-britain, the polities.csv slug for 1709-2024 (set by the reviewer am-08-x, 2026-10-19).

certainty.note: An island group: the coast is the frontier; the sovereignty dispute with Argentina does not change the drawn shape.

sources.title: History of the Falkland Islands
sources.note: 1811 Spanish garrison removed, 1820 Jewett, 1828-1831 Vernet, 3 January 1833, 1840-1845 colony and Stanley, 1982 invasion, 1985 Dependency split.

sources.title: Falkland Islands
sources.note: Infobox: area 12,173 km2, Stanley, British rule reasserted 3 January 1833, occupation 2 April to 14 June 1982, Dependencies from 1908 to 1985.

notes:
Cliopatria has no Falkland row. The History page says the United Provinces of the River Plate claimed the islands in 1820 (Jewett, 6 November 1820) and Vernet held East Falkland from 1828 under a grant; this dossier starts at the British reassertion on 3 January 1833. The Argentine side 1820-1833 is not a dossier of its own (rio-de-la-plata's Cliopatria shapes do not show the islands).
The end year 2024 is Cliopatria's last year (the state is alive). Antarctic parts of the Falkland Islands Dependencies (1908-1962: Graham Land, the South Orkneys and South Shetlands) are not on the pages opened; only South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands are drawn as dependencies, in vassal tint, from the History page's 1985 sentence. Port Louis is not in the gazetteer (coordinates approximate). South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands could be a small dossier of their own (suggested slug south-georgia-and-the-south-sandwich-islands).
